entries.proposition: DESIGN: 400 young-onset hypertensive Han Chinese patients from Taiwan matched to 400 normotensive controls, a gene-based scan built from marginal SNP p-values, RNA array in 12 extreme pairs, replication in a Hong Kong family study and a British case-control study.
entries.snippet: This TWNHS analyzed 400 matched pairs of patients with hypertension and normotensive controls.

entries.proposition: NO SNP-LEVEL SIGNAL: the single-SNP scan found no SNP at the stated thresholds; the gene-level hits are built from marginal SNPs.
entries.snippet: No significant SNPs (pFDR<10−3 or p<10−7) were found.

entries.proposition: WWOX NUMBERS: the gene-based p-values are 7.47 x 10 to the minus 14 (quoted FDR 5.77 x 10 to the minus 3) in the continuous-coding model and 1.18 x 10 to the minus 8 with BMI adjustment; the nominal-coding raw p-values are 0.017 and 0.022; the expression test gives p 5.96 x 10 to the minus 3 in 12 pairs.
entries.snippet: WWOX, which encodes the WW domain-containing protein on 16q23.3-q24.1, is the third gene that was simultaneously identified by our genome-wide GBAS

entries.proposition: REPLICATION IS WITHIN ANCESTRY: no gene was significantly confirmed in the British case-control data; WWOX is replicated only in the Hong Kong Han Chinese family study.
entries.snippet: Although no genes identified by us were significantly confirmed by the WTCCCHS data (Caucasian)

entries.proposition: CIRCULARITY OF THE EXPRESSION TEST: the 12 pairs for the array were chosen as the patients with the highest and controls with the lowest genotype risk scores from the same data, so the expression comparison is made on genotype-extreme samples.
entries.snippet: the 12 matched pairs of patients and controls were selected to have an extremely discordant genotypic distribution between groups

entries.proposition: MOUSE ANNOTATION AS MECHANISM: the article says WWOX variants are associated with hypoglycaemia, hyperphosphatemia, lower cholesterol and triglycerides and higher uric acid in mice; supplementary Table S2 shows these are Mouse Genome Informatics knockout phenotype terms, which also list postnatal lethality and abnormal adrenal gland morphology, not variant associations.
entries.snippet: WWOX variants are associated with hypoglycemia, hyperphosphatemia, decreased circulating cholesterol levels and triglyceride levels, but with increased blood uric acid levels in mice [59].

entries.proposition: CITATION MISMATCH: the text says WWOX variants were associated with blood pressure in a previous Japanese GWAS (reference 23), but Table 1 of the same article lists reference 23 as a European-ancestry study and the Japanese study with WWOX as reference 34.
entries.snippet: WWOX variants were also found to be associated with blood pressure in a previous Japanese GWAS [23].

entries.proposition: MECHANISM CLAIM: the Discussion states that IGF1, SLC4A4 and WWOX are primarily associated with obesity, glucose metabolism and ion homeostasis, well-known mechanisms of blood pressure regulation; no measurement of these in WWOX carriers is made in the article.
entries.snippet: are primarily associated with obesity, glucose metabolism, and ion homeostasis, which are well-known mechanisms of blood pressure regulation

entries.proposition: LIMITS: the three studies differ in phenotype definition (onset age 50 or younger only in the Taiwan cohort), arrays and populations.
entries.snippet: First, the phenotype definition and sample ascertainment were not exactly the same in the three studies (TWNHS, HKHS, and WTCCCHS).

entries.proposition: Figure 3A: in the cluster heatmap of the 17 genes the WWOX column groups with AP3S1, IGF1 and SFMBT1 and is red (higher) in the normotensive control rows and blue in most hypertensive rows; supplementary Table S3 gives a human beta of minus 0.248 (SE 0.071), i.e. lower expression in cases; the text gives no direction.
